dataset_name: Business Analysis Assistant compact full-system dev scenarios

usage.model_input: Initially pass only input.initial_requirements. Supply relevant conversation.prepared_answers as user replies when their topic is asked. Keep all expected fields outside model context.
usage.evaluation: All expectations are draft and require human review. Compare semantics and traceability, not exact JSON, wording or generated IDs. This dataset is scenario coverage, not evidence of measured system quality.
usage.splitting: All variants sharing group_id belong to the same split. All included cases are dev.
usage.scope: Full system: initial analysis, clarification, updated requirements, specification, task breakdown, acceptance criteria and RACI. Includes unresolved-conflict stopping behavior.
usage.conflicts: Two GAMMA-J scenarios without intended conflicts; two University Inventory scenarios with resolved or unresolved synthetic conflict.
usage.staged_evaluation: Components not yet implemented are reported as not_implemented. API errors are recorded as execution failures. Evaluate initial analysis independently and evaluate later components both with verified inputs and through the full journey when available.

provenance.adaptation: Unmodified supplied initial_requirements. Synthetic stakeholder replies and draft full-system evaluation checks added.

input.initial_requirements: GAMMA-J needs a web store that enables people who are new to online commerce to set up and operate an online retail business. Store owners and sales personnel should be able to manage products and customer accounts, while customers should be able to browse the available products, maintain a shopping cart, and place orders through the store.

goals_to_cover: Enable people new to online commerce to set up and operate an online retail business.
clarification_checks: Ask relevant questions tied to missing information; equivalent wording is acceptable.
Ask for project team roles and decision responsibilities needed to prepare RACI.
must_avoid: Do not infer payment methods, delivery rules, refunds, or inventory synchronization as confirmed requirements.
evidence_checks: Every extracted fact must be supported by an exact nonempty substring of the input.
The quoted text must support the full meaning and conditions of the associated description.

conversation.delivery_rule: Provide the relevant answer only after the assistant asks about its topic. Topic matching is by meaning, not generated question ID. A human operator routes the prepared answers. Never pass evaluation expectations to the assistant.

prepared_answers.text: The project team consists of a Product Owner, a Business Analyst, a Full-stack Developer, and a QA Engineer. The Product Owner defines priorities, approves business requirements, and makes the final release decision. The Business Analyst gathers and clarifies requirements, prepares the specification, and maintains links between requirements and implementation tasks. The Full-stack Developer makes technical implementation decisions, develops the application, and deploys releases. The QA Engineer prepares and executes tests, records defects, and reports whether the release meets the agreed acceptance criteria. The Product Owner approves the user acceptance testing results.

The first release serves one store. Customers may browse without signing in but must sign in before placing an order. Customers can add available products to the cart, change quantities to positive whole numbers, and remove items. Store owners and sales personnel can create and update products and customer accounts. Orders are submitted for staff processing; online payments and shipping integrations are outside the first release. A successful submission creates one order containing the selected items and quantities and displays its reference. An empty cart cannot be submitted. The business goal is to let store staff receive and process orders without manually transcribing customer messages. The Product Owner accepts the first release when the agreed browse-cart-order flow passes user acceptance testing. The first release is due eight weeks after requirements approval. Store owner is the Product Owner for this project.

The Product Owner is accountable for specification acceptance and user acceptance testing. The Business Analyst is responsible for preparing the specification. The Full-stack Developer is accountable for implementation and deployment. The QA Engineer is accountable for test execution. The Product Owner is accountable for the final release decision.

input.initial_requirements:
A university needs a Unified University Inventory System that combines the inventory databases of three faculties and makes the integrated inventory available through a secure web interface. University, faculty, and department staff need to manage assets such as rooms, software licences, and equipment, while other users should be able to request assets or reserve spaces for approval by the appropriate administrative level.

The project team consists of a Product Owner, a Business Analyst, a Full-stack Developer, and a QA Engineer. The Product Owner defines priorities, approves business requirements, and makes the final release decision. The Business Analyst gathers and clarifies requirements, prepares the specification, and maintains links between requirements and implementation tasks. The Full-stack Developer makes technical implementation decisions, develops the application, and deploys releases. The QA Engineer prepares and executes tests, records defects, and reports whether the release meets the agreed acceptance criteria. A faculty inventory representative explains asset request and space reservation workflows and participates in user acceptance testing. The Product Owner approves the user acceptance testing results.

Every room reservation must be approved by the owning faculty administrator before confirmation. Every room reservation is confirmed immediately without administrator approval.

users_to_cover: Other users requesting assets or reserving spaces
requirement_meanings_to_cover: Provide integrated inventory through a secure web interface.
Manage assets including rooms, software licences and equipment.
Support approval by the appropriate administrative level.

Every room reservation is confirmed immediately without administrator approval.

prepared_answers.text: Every room reservation requires approval by the owning faculty administrator before confirmation. Withdraw the immediate confirmation rule.

The first release integrates inventory from three faculties and allows university members to request assets and reserve rooms. Members sign in using their university accounts. Faculty staff maintain assets belonging to their faculty. University staff can view all faculties. Department staff can view their department assets. Each request or room reservation is approved by the administrator of the faculty that owns the asset; approval is required before confirmation. A room cannot have overlapping confirmed reservations. Start and end times use the Europe/Kyiv time zone and the end must be later than the start. A rejected request remains visible to its requester with a rejected status. University staff resolve duplicate source records manually before import; the prototype does not automatically merge ambiguous duplicates. The goal is to provide a shared view of inventory and a clear request approval workflow. The Product Owner accepts the release after the agreed inventory and reservation scenarios pass user acceptance testing. The first release is due eight weeks after requirements approval.

The Product Owner is accountable for specification acceptance and user acceptance testing. The Business Analyst is responsible for preparing the specification. The Full-stack Developer is accountable for implementation and deployment. The QA Engineer is accountable for test execution. The Product Owner is accountable for the final release decision.
